harmonicFunction.title: Sound Characteristics
harmonicFunction.description: Very harsh and dissonant. Creates strong urge to resolve. Sounds "crunchy" or "gritty." Almost like two notes fighting each other.

harmonicFunction.title: Memory Aid
harmonicFunction.description: Think of the minor 2nd as the sound of suspense in a horror movie - it's the musical equivalent of tension that demands resolution. The theme from "Jaws" features prominent minor 2nds that create that sense of impending danger. In classical music, it's often called a "semitone" and is fundamental to chromatic harmony and voice leading.

historicalDevelopment.title: Natural Semitones on Guitar
historicalDevelopment.description: E to F: Open 1st string (high E) to 1st fret = minor 2nd. B to C: Open 2nd string (B) to 1st fret = minor 2nd. These are the only natural minor 2nds (no sharps/flats needed).

historicalDevelopment.title: Adjacent Frets Rule
historicalDevelopment.description: Universal Rule: Any two adjacent frets on the same string form a minor 2nd. Examples: 3rd fret to 4th fret, 7th fret to 8th fret, etc. This makes minor 2nds the easiest interval to find on guitar!

relatedIntervals.title: Ascending Minor 2nds
relatedIntervals.description: E (open) → F (1st fret), G# (4th fret) → A (5th fret)
relatedIntervals.detail: A (open) → A# (1st fret), E (open) → F (1st fret) on high E string

relatedIntervals.title: Harmonic Minor 2nds (Dissonance)
relatedIntervals.description: Playing minor 2nds simultaneously creates maximum harmonic tension
relatedIntervals.detail: Rarely used in traditional harmony except as passing tones or for special effect. Used in modern classical and jazz for color.

relatedIntervals.title: Chromatic Scale Foundation
relatedIntervals.description: The minor 2nd is the building block of the chromatic scale
relatedIntervals.detail: Every fret on guitar represents one minor 2nd, making it the fundamental unit of pitch distance
